title: January ENSO gave no clear added February-April precipitation forecast gain in seven California divisions in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether January Nino 3.4 improves February-April precipitation forecasts beyond November-January local precipitation. We used fixed NOAA ERSSTv5 and nClimDiv data. Each linear fit used only earlier years. In South Coast Drainage, the planned endpoint, mean squared error fell by 17.05%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -26.49% to 40.21%. RMSE fell from 123.90 to 112.84 mm. All seven division intervals included zero. The South Coast gain was 30.51% in 1981-2003 and -14.86% in 2004-2025. January instead of October-December Nino 3.4 gave a 1.94% error reduction, with an interval of -5.07% to 9.27%. These results do not establish a stable forecast gain. This study adds a late-winter benchmark to earlier campaign tests of summer and autumn predictors. It does not discover a new ENSO link or test a physical cause. Revised data, release delays, short records and conditional uncertainty limit the result. Code, forecasts, source hashes, data retrieval instructions, numerical checks and a figure are included.

display.caption: January ENSO gives uncertain MSE reductions beyond November-January local precipitation in seven California divisions. Limits use fixed forecasts and paired five-year blocks. South Coast cumulative error gains weaken after 1998.
